hints: Keep each value's original one-based position before sorting.
For each value, search for target-value among values that appear later in the sorted order.
Return the two original positions, making sure they are distinct.
analogy: Sort labeled cards by value; for each card, look for the complement while keeping the labels.
example: For values 2,7,5,1 and target 8, the values 7 and 1 have original positions 2 and 4.
algorithm: Sort pairs (value,index). Use two pointers from both ends; if their sum is too small move left up, if too large move right down, and on equality print indices.
correctness: The ordering makes sums monotone as either pointer moves, so each discarded pair of possibilities cannot be a solution; stored labels recover the required positions.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space for indexed sorted pairs.
